title: Memory Brokering & Contingency Plan for KV/Activation Budgeting under Continuous Batching
creator: Aparna Rao
description:
Problem: As continuous batching scales across mixed-tenant workloads, ephemeral activation + KV cache allocations cause unpredictable per-GPU memory pressure. Current hard watermarks and global evictions result in noisy tail latency and occasional preemption of high-priority requests.

Goal: Implement a memory brokering layer and contingency ledger to allocate and reconcile headroom across weights, activations, and KV slots. The broker should provide per-tenant soft guarantees (burst credits + decay), slot leasing for large KV fetches, and a contingency policy that gracefully degrades to quantized model variants or throttled batching when headroom is exhausted.

Scope: Runtime changes (broker, slot-leasing hooks, eviction policy), scheduler integration (batch cadence smoothing signal), telemetry (per-tenant ledger metrics and eviction provenance), and rollout plan with canary and guardrails. This ticket covers design, PoC implementation, integration tests, and a canary rollout on a dedicated pool.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce a memory broker API that tracks per-GPU ledgers for weights, KV, and activations and exposes remaining headroom as a numeric credit
Slot leasing implemented: large KV load requests can request short-lived leases and be charged burst credits; leases reclaim on early termination
Contingency policy executes when broker reports < 7% free headroom: prefer low-latency degrades (evict cold-KV ranges, compact KV entries) before model-variant fallback
Telemetry surface: per-tenant daily/5m charts for ledger balance, lease usage, eviction reasons, and OOM events
Canary rollout with traffic shaping results in <=1.2x baseline 95p latency and eviction-induced errors < 0.5% of requests
tasks: Design and document memory brokering API and ledger data model (confluence doc)
Implement in-runtime broker with lightweight atomic counters and periodic reconciliation
Add slot-leasing protocol to KV fetch path and batch scheduler hooks
Implement contingency policy actions: cold-KV compaction, soft eviction windows, quantized-model fallback path
Add telemetry probes and tracing for eviction provenance and lease accounting
Create unit/integration tests that simulate mixed-tenant spike scenarios
Run canary on dedicated gpu-pool-priv-03 and monitor metrics for 72 hours
Produce runbook for on-call with mitigation steps and dashboard links
progress_updates: 2026-02-20: Internal design synced with runtime and scheduler leads. Agreed on simple ledger schema: {weights_reserved, kv_reserved, activations_reserved, burst_credits}. Decided ledger reconciliation to run every 250ms.
2026-02-26: PoC broker implemented with atomic slot counters. Early tests show broker API adds <1% CPU overhead per worker and reconciles within 5ms on p4d-style node.

2026-03-03: Slot-leasing integrated into KV fetch path; observed reduction in synchronous eviction events during artificial KV storm test. Need to refine lease expiry jitter and backpressure signal to batch scheduler.
2026-03-09: Contingency policy prototype completed. Preliminary canary window scheduled for 2026-03-18 on gpu-pool-priv-03 with traffic shaping to 5% of production.
Next: finalize telemetry naming conventions, add provenance tags to eviction traces, and add canary alert thresholds.
comments: Liam Chen (2026-02-21): Good direction. Two quick asks: include a metric for reclaimed bytes by action type and ensure lease accounting survives process restart.
Diego Martinez (2026-02-28): PoC looks promising. Noted a race when two leases overlap on the same KV range under concurrent prefetch — added task to add per-range optimistic locking.
Priya Nair (SRE) (2026-03-04): For the runbook please specify exact PagerDuty playbook and a fallback to route traffic to dedicated low-latency pool if canary shows >1.5x tail latency.
Aparna Rao (2026-03-09): Approved canary. Ensure we have an automatic rollback if eviction-induced errors exceed 0.5% over a 15m window.
risks: Incorrect credit decay rates could starve bursty low-latency tenants or conversely allow noisy neighbors to monopolize KV slots
Lease bookkeeping must be resilient to worker restarts to avoid double-counting and leaking headroom
Aggressive compaction/eviction may increase downstream tail latency if requests trigger re-fetches
rollout_plan: Stage 0: deploy broker and telemetry to staging, run stress harness for mixed-tenant KV storms
Stage 1 (Canary): deploy to gpu-pool-priv-03 at 5% of traffic for 72 hours, monitor ledger balance and eviction provenance
Stage 2: increase to 20% traffic with feature flags and observe 7-day stability window
Stage 3: global rollout with gradual enablement per-region and automated rollback if thresholds breached
runbook_summary: On alarm (eviction_error_rate > 0.5% or 95p latency > 1.5x baseline): 1) disable new slot leases via feature flag; 2) trigger soft-eviction-runbook to compact cold KV ranges; 3) route high-priority traffic to dedicated low-latency pool; 4) rollback runtime change if remediation fails
notes: This design intentionally separates headroom accounting from weight residency bookkeeping to keep model weights immutable at load time. The broker focuses on volatile allocations (KV + activations + transient prefetch buffers) and provides the scheduler coarse-grained signals for batch cadence smoothing.
